assessments.scope: QuALITY HARD hidden-information reading comprehension with verified quotes; RLHF-tuned 2023-2024 models (GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude 2.1, Claude 1.3, Mixtral 8x7B debaters; GPT-4-Turbo, Mixtral-8x7B, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude 2.1 LLM judges; 21 retained human judges); the accuracies reported in arXiv:2402.06782v4

conditions: The experiment is recorded as the paper reports it; no replication, code or data was examined.

The LLM-judge and human-judge accuracies come from different arms: the reading record gives the LLM experiments the TL 400 train and DL 291 development splits and the human experiments the TH 153 and DH 47 splits, and names GPT-4-Turbo best-of-16 debaters for the main human experiment, so the claim's list of five debaters does not describe the debaters behind the human-judge 88%, 60% and 78%. The best-of-16 detail is an AI reading awaiting the human check in review card rows R2-R5.

Human judgement counts as read by the AI, unverified by a human: 953 test-batch and 2,362 iteration judgements (3,315 together, matching the Fig. 29 caption as read) and a 6,476 total in the text as read; the human check decides whether these describe one count.

The observation states that the main human experiments used GPT-4-Turbo best-of-16 debaters, not all five debater models the claim lists (GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude 2.1, Claude 1.3 and Mixtral 8x7B), and it covers only the claim's human-judge values, not its LLM-judge values (76%, naive 48%, consultancy 54%, expert judge 92.5%).
